input.rationale: Trace how a restarted node re-establishes its configuration ('context validity') when the committed-log replay feature is enabled. NewRaft replays committed logs first (restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index) and then scans the log for configuration entries starting at max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1. Because the scan is skipped over the committed prefix, configuration entries inside it are never applied to r.configurations when no snapshot carries them, even though they remain in the log. Focused probe: restart a single-voter node that was bootstrapped and applied commands but never snapshotted, with RestoreCommittedLogs on/off and with a covering snapshot as control.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, whose newest configuration entry is inside the persisted commit index and has no covering snapshot, still know that configuration after NewRaft returns?
investigations.hypothesis: No. restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so the configuration scan starts after the committed prefix and never calls processConfigurationLogEntry for the configuration entry that only exists in the log. r.configurations.latest stays empty (or stays at the snapshot configuration), so the node loses its own membership context, cannot start elections, and skips the membership checks when granting votes.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same durable state twice: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and with RestoreCommittedLogs=false. Predict servers_after=0 and no re-election with the feature on, versus servers_after=1 and a successful re-election with it off. A third run takes a snapshot before restart to show that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss (servers_after=1), separating the scanning bound from generic restart damage.

gaps.question: When a snapshot exists but the newest configuration entry was committed after that snapshot (ConfigurationIndex older than the entry), does the same skipped committed prefix make the restarted node adopt the older configuration, permanently losing the newer membership (and its quorum size), and does that stale configuration later justify a different decision or duty completion?

interpretations.rationale: Observed in the retained execution: after restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot, the node's configuration is empty (event index 1: mode=restore_on_no_snapshot, servers_before=1, servers_after=0, config_preserved=false, snapshot_count=0, staged_commit=6, log_last_index=7) and it never campaigns again (became_leader=false after a 3s opportunity, with the node logging 'no known peers, aborting election'), while the two controls keep the configuration and re-elect (index 3 restore_off_no_snapshot: servers_after=1, became_leader=true; index 5 restore_on_with_snapshot: servers_after=1, snapshot_count=1, became_leader=true). Source account of the mechanism: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755) and the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never turned into r.configurations by their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty, runFollower refuses to start an election (raft.go 230-234) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by the retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: after a snapshot that carries configuration {A,B}@1, a committed AddVoter C at index 8 and four further commits (staged commit 11), the restarted node reports servers_after=2 while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still contains the newest configuration entry at index 8 (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1). That stale base then changes a real decision: a later AddVoter E against the restarted node returned no error and the cluster converged on 3 members with contains_c_final=false on both nodes (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3), i.e. voter C was silently removed although no request removed it. The control run in the same receipt with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 members and ended with 4 members including C (observed at parsed index 5, whose comparison the controller recorded as unknown because both modes emit the same result event name).

counterevidence: The control mode inside the same receipt (parsed index 5) kept servers_after=3 and the later change produced 4 members including C, so the stale base is specific to the replayed committed prefix rather than to snapshots or configuration changes in general.
The restarted node still held every committed entry on disk (log_last_index=12), so this is lost configuration context, not lost data; the entry would be re-read only from a snapshot install.
limitations: The control mod in the same receipt was scored 'unknown' by the controller because both modes emit the same result event name; its observed values at index 5 are cited as observations, and the dedicated control experiment requested in this update is meant to produce an independently scored control.
Voter C never runs in this probe, so the probe does not show whether C itself would notice the removal; the finding is about the configuration each running node decides with.
Executed scope is two in-memory voters at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts and one committed single-server change; joint consensus and multi-step changes are not exercised.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts belong to the same question and harness family (single-voter restart probe, then two-voter snapshot/configuration-change probe) executed from the same snapshot; the second probe was built after the first receipt confirmed the empty-configuration case, to test whether a snapshot-carried configuration makes the loss stale rather than empty, and whether that stale base changes a later decision.

interpretations.rationale: Registered gap answered by source trace plus a construction-time run of this probe. Source: a restarted node adopts the snapshot's configuration whenever the newest configuration entry lies inside the skipped committed prefix (api.go 611-613 with 723-755, snapshot path api.go 645-689), and appendConfigurationEntry then computes the next configuration from that stale r.configurations.latest (raft.go 1204-1241) once configurationChangeChIfStable admits the change because latest and committed indexes look equal (raft.go 654-664); nextConfiguration derives the new membership from that same base (configuration.go 328-406). Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 servers and the later change produced 4 members including C.

Source dependency chain recorded in the rationale; construction-time run reproduced all three predictions, retained execution pending.

counterevidence: The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores preserved all three members and added E without dropping C, so the stale base is specific to the skipped committed prefix rather than to config changes in general.
limitations: This is a construction-time native reproduction; the formal receipt for this harness is requested in this update and the claim is retained as explained/unresolved-for-receipt until it exists.
C never runs, so the probe cannot show whether C would itself notice or resist its removal; that is about C's own state, not about the decision the restarted node made.

The removal happens through a successful public AddVoter, so the consequence is reachable through the ordinary configuration API, but only while the restarted node is leader and its stale latest/committed indexes look equal.

excluded: No multi-voter cluster, no configuration change, no partitions.

experiment.prefix: Real bootstrap, real election, real applies, real shutdown and restart on the same durable stores with a fresh transport; no fabricated log entries or configuration state.

scope.description: In-process single-voter Cluster: bootstrap a configuration entry, become leader, apply five commands, then restart the node on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with a fresh transport. Three cases: restore_committed_logs on with no snapshot; off with no snapshot; on with a snapshot taken before the restart. Observations are the node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), whether it reaches Leader again, applied/commit indices, and staged commit index at restart.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs is a documented public Config field (config.go 243-254) that is enabled by the application; the probe only supplies that documented configuration.
The existing test TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs always snapshots before restarting (raft_test.go 1183-1280), so the configuration-in-log path is not covered by it.
No snapshot is taken in the no-snapshot cases (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m), which is normal operation for clusters below the snapshot threshold.
excluded: Multi-node clusters and network partitions: the probe is a single-voter cluster, so the observed election abort is a progress loss and the vote-check consequence is source-read, not executed here.

basis.prefix: Fresh in-memory transport, InmemCommitTrackingStore log store, InmemStore stable store, InmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster writes the single-voter configuration at index 1/term 1; first NewRaft elects the node as leader; five Apply commands are committed; optional user snapshot; Shutdown; second NewRaft on the same stores with a new transport sharing the same address. The harness never fabricates log entries or configuration state: all durable state comes from real bootstrap, real elections, real commits and a real snapshot.

comparisons.description: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, the restarted node must still report the bootstrapped voter.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration, isolating the committed-prefix replay as the cause.

scope.description: Two-voter in-memory cluster {A,B}: A is bootstrapped with both voters and becomes leader, commands are committed, A takes a snapshot (configuration {A,B} at index 1), then AddVoter C commits a configuration entry at index 8 while A and B are the only running servers. Four further commands push the persisted commit index past index 8. A is shut down and restarted on the same stores with a fresh transport (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false). Observed: the restarted node's configuration membership versus the still-running peer's view and the newest configuration entry in its own log; then, while the restarted node is stably leader, one further AddVoter E and the resulting cluster configuration on both nodes.
assumptions: AddVoter C commits with acks from A and B only, which is a legal quorum of three voters; C is never started, so nothing else can observe C's absence.
The snapshot predates the configuration change, so it carries configuration {A,B} at index 1 while the newest configuration entry (index 8) is in the log.
The extra commands after the change are ordinary applications; they only advance the persisted commit index past the configuration entry, which any later commit would do.
excluded: Elections, partitions and failover among more than two servers are not exercised; the point is which configuration each node uses, not how leaders are chosen.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap of both voters on A, real election, real applies, real user snapshot on A, real AddVoter C through the cluster, real shutdown and restart of A on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore. Nothing is fabricated: the log, snapshot metadata and staged commit index all come from those operations, and the control case runs the identical procedure with RestoreCommittedLogs=false.

comparisons.description: After restart with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, the node must still know the newest committed configuration {A,B,C} that is present in its own log.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps all three members.
A configuration change issued by the restarted node must not remove voter C, which no request removed and which remains in the committed configuration.

interpretations.rationale: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); nothing waives configuration recovery. The code nevertheless bounds the configuration scan by max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613) while restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755). processConfigurationLogEntry is the only path that turns a log entry into r.configurations (raft.go 1605-1623), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are dropped whenever a snapshot does not carry them (snapshot path: api.go 645-689). Consequence: after a plain restart of a bootstrapped node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, r.configurations.latest is empty, so runFollower refuses to campaign ('no known peers', raft.go 230-234) and both requestVote and requestPreVote skip their membership checks because they are gated on a non-empty Servers list (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784). The rule that decides the decision is therefore evaluated against an empty configuration rather than the replicated one.
counterevidence: The existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes: it always snapshots before restarting, so its configuration comes from snapshot metadata rather than from the log, and the same probe shows that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss.

The loss is not caused by the commit-tracking store or by replaying logs to the FSM per se: the control restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores and log contents keeps the configuration and wins the election again.
limitations: The executed probe is a single-voter in-memory cluster; the multi-node consequences (a node that grants votes to servers it cannot be shown to contain, or a node whose quorum size is computed from a stale configuration) are read from source, not executed.

The persisted commit index used at restart is what the store reported (6 while the log ended at 7); the drop of the configuration entry does not depend on that lag, but the exact boundary of what is skipped does.
Whether upstream intends applications to always snapshot before enabling this option is not stated anywhere in the captured sources; the Config documentation mentions no such requirement.

Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 servers and the later change produced 4 members including C.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Yes for both parts, subject to the retained receipt for this probe: the stale configuration is adopted when the snapshot predates the committed configuration entry, and it does justify a different decision - a configuration change based on the stale membership drops voter C for the whole cluster (observed change_err=nil, both nodes ending with 3 members and contains_c=false), instead of the intended 4-member configuration. Source dependency chain recorded in the rationale; construction-time run reproduced all three predictions, retained execution pending.

counterevidence: The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores preserved all three members and added E without dropping C, so the stale base is specific to the skipped committed prefix rather than to config changes in general.
limitations: This is a construction-time native reproduction; the formal receipt for this harness is requested in this update and the claim is retained as explained/unresolved-for-receipt until it exists.
C never runs, so the probe cannot show whether C would itself notice or resist its removal; that is about C's own state, not about the decision the restarted node made.

The removal happens through a successful public AddVoter, so the consequence is reachable through the ordinary configuration API, but only while the restarted node is leader and its stale latest/committed indexes look equal.

interpretations.rationale: Observed in the retained execution: after restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot, the node's configuration is empty (event index 1: mode=restore_on_no_snapshot, servers_before=1, servers_after=0, config_preserved=false, snapshot_count=0, staged_commit=6, log_last_index=7) and it never campaigns again (became_leader=false after a 3s opportunity, with the node logging 'no known peers, aborting election'), while the two controls keep the configuration and re-elect (index 3 restore_off_no_snapshot: servers_after=1, became_leader=true; index 5 restore_on_with_snapshot: servers_after=1, snapshot_count=1, became_leader=true). Source account of the mechanism: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755) and the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never turned into r.configurations by their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty, runFollower refuses to start an election (raft.go 230-234) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by the retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: after a snapshot that carries configuration {A,B}@1, a committed AddVoter C at index 8 and four further commits (staged commit 11), the restarted node reports servers_after=2 while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still contains the newest configuration entry at index 8 (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1). That stale base then changes a real decision: a later AddVoter E against the restarted node returned no error and the cluster converged on 3 members with contains_c_final=false on both nodes (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3), i.e. voter C was silently removed although no request removed it. The control run in the same receipt with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 members and ended with 4 members including C (observed at parsed index 5, whose comparison the controller recorded as unknown because both modes emit the same result event name).

counterevidence: The control mode inside the same receipt (parsed index 5) kept servers_after=3 and the later change produced 4 members including C, so the stale base is specific to the replayed committed prefix rather than to snapshots or configuration changes in general.
The restarted node still held every committed entry on disk (log_last_index=12), so this is lost configuration context, not lost data; the entry would be re-read only from a snapshot install.
limitations: The control mod in the same receipt was scored 'unknown' by the controller because both modes emit the same result event name; its observed values at index 5 are cited as observations, and the dedicated control experiment requested in this update is meant to produce an independently scored control.
Voter C never runs in this probe, so the probe does not show whether C itself would notice the removal; the finding is about the configuration each running node decides with.
Executed scope is two in-memory voters at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts and one committed single-server change; joint consensus and multi-step changes are not exercised.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts belong to the same question and harness family (single-voter restart probe, then two-voter snapshot/configuration-change probe) executed from the same snapshot; the second probe was built after the first receipt confirmed the empty-configuration case, to test whether a snapshot-carried configuration makes the loss stale rather than empty, and whether that stale base changes a later decision.
